title: Change a press to the die that clears its hidden punch
instruction: Rack the old die, change the press to the die that clears its punch, cycle it with its guard on, and move both hands away.
context: Setters changing tooling on a press have to match the die to the punch that's actually fitted. Bringing a punch down on a die that doesn't clear it wrecks both.
setup: Station table. A small press stands with its bed's centre at (31, 0) cm: a black steel bed 16 x 19 cm, 2 cm thick, runs from 10 cm in front of that centre to 6 cm behind it, with steel side rails 15.8 cm apart and 1.2 cm tall, starting 1.5 cm in front of the centre, a rear stop 2.5 cm behind the centre, and steel columns at each side 10 cm tall. A sprung blue ram travels 3 cm straight down, about 1 N at the top and 2.5 N at the bottom, pressed by a 6 x 6 cm pad to the +y side of the press, 9.5 cm above the table at rest. Its orange 3 cm square punch has its tip 5.3 cm above the table at rest; the lot sets it across the press, +5 cm, 0 or -5 cm in y. A loose grey ABS guard 8 x 19 cm, 6 mm thick, 100 g, with a 3 x 2.5 cm grip 2.4 cm tall at its middle, lies on the columns over the ram and hides the punch from above. In the press sits a solid dark aluminium die, 335 g. Three bare aluminium dies, 310 g each, lie on the table with their centres of pocket at (17.2, 0), (17.2, -16) and (17.2, +16) cm. Every die is a plate 16 cm long in x and 15 cm wide, 5 mm thick, with a hollow 3 x 3 cm grip 4.5 cm tall on top, 5.9 cm in front of the pocket's place; the plate reaches 2.5 cm behind that place. Each bare die has one closed 4 cm square pocket through it, at +5 cm in y on the die at y 0, at 0 on the die at -16, and at -5 cm on the die at +16. A yellow rack mat 17 x 17 cm, 2 mm thick, lies with its centre at (28.5, -20) cm. Positions are from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, with +y toward the left arm. The screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read at the end of the run. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint. 0 for good if the punch ever touches any die's plate (within 0.5 mm), at any insertion, or if the ram makes a full stroke (2.7 cm or more) without the guard on; 0 if any part is off the table. The guard is on when it's flat within 5 degrees, within 2 cm of its place in x and y and within 4 mm in height, with both hands 5 cm or more from its grip. Otherwise 0 unless the old die lies flat on the rack, its plate's centre within 3 cm of the rack's centre in x and y, its underside within 1 cm of the rack's top, and both hands 5 cm from its grip. Then 0.1. 0.5 if the die whose pocket clears the punch is also home on the bed: within 4 mm of the rear stop's position in x, 5 mm of the centre line, 3 mm of the bed's height, square and flat within 5 degrees, with both hands 5 cm from its grip. 0.8 if the press has also made a full stroke with the old die racked, that die home and the guard on, and now the guard is on, the ram is within 3 mm of the top, and both hands are 8 cm or more from the pad and from every part's grip. 1.0 if all that's been at rest (parts under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, the ram under 1 cm/s) for the last 1 s. A stroke with an empty bed and the guard on costs nothing. Trials are run on each of lots A to C and averaged.
reset_notes: Set the dies, guard and ram back as in the screenshot. Nothing is consumed. Lots use a different punch position.
fidelity: A rigid-body simulation with square parts for stable contact and a USD spring for the ram. There's no sheet metal, cutting force or damage: touching metal with the punch is only scored. Dies are light, thin aluminium, with grips set at their balance points so parallel fingers can carry them. The press is small and its stroke short, to fit the arms' reach. The punch shows about 6 pixels wide from the top camera at 320x176 once the guard is off.
